# Classes

## Graphic Standards Manual

Week 1. Set up the graphic system you will use to present all your later work.

- [Class 01]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-01/) — Week 1 — Aug 25: Begin the Graphic Standards Manual, test a sample sheet and organize your files.

<a id="b02"></a>

## Constructive Solid Geometry

Weeks 2–3. Build solids you can keep editing, using move, rotate, scale and Boolean operations.

- [Class 02 · Transformations and Booleans]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-02/) — Week 2 — Sep 1: Move, rotate and scale with nodes. Compare the solid Boolean operations and begin the massing study.
- [Class 03 · 3D printing]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-03/) — Week 3 — Sep 8: Refine the CSG process sheet and instructions. P2b starts: prepare the CSG object for 3D printing — units, orientation and slicing.

<a id="b03"></a>

## Descriptive Geometry

Weeks 4–5. Describe geometry as points, lines, edges and faces, then build a solid you control with parameters.

- [Class 04 · Point to solid]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-04/) — Week 4 — Sep 15: Point → Line → Edge → Face → Solid → Boolean. Build the parametric pyramid and reconnect to the CSG project.
- [Class 05 · Your module, material and lighting]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-05/) — Week 5 — Sep 22: Build your own module from points and faces, test its parameter ranges, then render it with one material and a considered lighting setup for the P3a sheet.

<a id="b04"></a>

## Arrays 1 — line, grid, cube, curve

Week 6. First of two Arrays classes. Build a row, a grid and a layered array with loops and nested loops, then bend the row onto a curve. Name the count, spacing and index in each direction.

- [Class 06]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-06/) — Week 6 — Sep 29: Build a loop and a nested loop — a 1D row, a 2D grid, then 3D layers — then bend the row onto a curve. Name the count, spacing and index in each direction. Check your CSG print file before queueing it.

<a id="b04-second"></a>

## Arrays 2 — if/Switch in 2D and 3D

Week 7. Second of two Arrays classes. Patterns start with a brick wall where every other course shifts; then if/Switch rules make façade patterns, and the same rules, reading the layer index, make 3D patterns in an array of cubes. Hexagonal and radial arrays and math-shaped volumes are optional.

- Class 07 — *not yet released* — Week 7 — Oct 6: Use Compare and Switch to select between façade patterns — a brick wall with every other course shifted is the first example — then apply the same rules in 3D, using the layer index as well as rows and columns. Start from small examples; hexagonal and radial arrays and math-shaped volumes are optional. No graded submission this week (studio reviews).

<a id="b04-support"></a>

## Supported practice — Arrays 1 and 2

Week 8. Supported practice, no new topic. Bring all three array sheets for feedback on repetition, index, counts and spacing, your if/Switch patterns in 2D and 3D, and anything still open before everything through Arrays is due on Sunday, October 18 at 11:59 PM.

- Class 08 — *not yet released* — Week 8 — Oct 13: Supported practice; nothing is due. Bring all three array sheets and anything still open from 1, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1: check the loops, counts and spacing of your 1D/2D/3D arrays and your if/Switch patterns in 2D and 3D, and fix problems before everything is due on Sunday, October 18 at 11:59 PM. No new topic.

<a id="b04-review"></a>

## Pin-up and grading — everything through Arrays

Week 9. Everything through Arrays, submitted by Sunday, October 18 at 11:59 PM, is pinned up: the manual, 2.1, 2.2 with the physical print, 3.1 and 3.2. No new topic; façade attractors start the following week.

- Class 09 — *not yet released* — Week 9 — Oct 20: Pin-up and grading of everything through Arrays — the manual (1), 2.1, 2.2, 3.1 and 3.2 — submitted by Sunday, October 18 at 11:59 PM. Bring the physical 2.2 print. No new topic. Façade attractors start next week.

<a id="b05"></a>

## Façade attractors — Project 3

Week 10. One class on façade attractors. Combine one curve and one or two point attractors to drive one panel dimension. You use attractors again for site analysis in Project 4.

- Class 10 — *not yet released* — Week 10 — Oct 27: Façade attractors for 3.3: combine one curve and one or two points to drive a panel parameter, then begin the elevation and isometric composition.

<a id="b06"></a>

## Attractor-based site analysis — Project 4

Week 11. Apply attractor measurements to the prepared point cloud with the supplied groups. Make two analysis layers and one design observation for the final project. This class is separate from the façade class.

- Class 11 — *not yet released* — Week 11 — Nov 3: Start 4.1 with the prepared point cloud and supplied analysis groups: use attractor measurements to make two analysis layers and one design observation. The class also maps out Project 4, from analysis to laser-cut model, with brief individual feedback on your façade.

<a id="b06-volume"></a>

## Generative volume exploration — Project 4

Week 12. Use the supplied volume groups to explore three settings of one strategy, and choose a form for contouring.

- Class 12 — *not yet released* — Week 12 — Nov 10: 4.2 starts with supplied volume groups: explore three settings of one generative strategy and choose one isometric result. Bring your two site-analysis layers — the check is how they connect to the volume.

<a id="b07"></a>

## Contouring, laser-cut preparation and assembly

Week 13. The last class with new required content, taught through a prepared example with the supplied contouring group: spacing, numbered parts, preparing cutting files, material and kerf tests, registration (how the parts line up), simple assembly and final documentation. 4.3 and 4.4 are introduced here and produced in Weeks 14–15.

- Class 13 · Last new topic — *not yet released* — Week 13 — Nov 17: Submit 3.3. Bring your chosen volume. 4.3 and 4.4 start with a worked example of the full fabrication process: the supplied contouring group, spacing, numbered cutting layouts, material and kerf tests, registration (how the parts line up), simple assembly and documentation. You refine your own work in Weeks 14–15. This is the last class with new required content.

<a id="b08"></a>

## Production, feedback and documentation

Weeks 14–15. No new required content. Week 14 checks contours and assembly tests. Week 15 checks fabrication progress and one booklet spread and supports production, revisions and final documentation during studio reviews; nothing is graded that day.

- Class 14 · Contours and assembly tests — *not yet released* — Week 14 — Nov 24: Submit 4.1. Bring numbered contours, the cutting layout, an assembly diagram and a small material or registration test. Refine files and begin production with individual feedback. No new topic.
- Class 15 · Laser-cut assembly and final documentation — *not yet released* — Week 15 — Dec 1: No graded submission during studio reviews. Ungraded check: bring tested samples, cutting progress, your assembly and a plan for the remaining work, plus one booklet spread for fabrication and presentation feedback. Help with connections, part files and final documentation.
